provisions.title: Colorado Privacy Act, duty regarding sensitive data
provisions.quote: A controller shall not process or sell a consumer's sensitive data without first obtaining the consumer's consent
provisions.appliesTo: Satisfies one or both of the following thresholds: controls or processes the personal data of one hundred thousand consumers or more during a calendar year; or derives revenue or receives a discount on the price of goods or services from the sale of personal data and processes or controls the personal data of twenty-five thousand consumers or more

provisions.title: Colorado Privacy Act, applicability of part
provisions.quote: controls or processes the personal data of one hundred thousand consumers or more during a calendar year; or derives revenue or receives a discount on the price of goods or services from the sale of personal data and processes or controls the personal data of twenty-five thousand consumers or more
provisions.appliesTo: Controllers that conduct business in Colorado or target Colorado residents and meet the thresholds; any amount of biometric data also brings a controller in (6-1-1304(1)(a)(II)).

provisions.title: SB 25-276 (signed act), section 20 amending 6-1-1308(7)
provisions.quote: A controller shall not process OR SELL a consumer's sensitive data without first obtaining the consumer's consent
provisions.appliesTo: Same controllers as 6-1-1304.

consumer_health_data.note: Colorado Privacy Act requires opt-in consent to process or sell sensitive data, which includes a mental or physical health condition or diagnosis. No dedicated consumer health data law found in title 6. Thresholds apply.

crossCheck.note: Quotes, citations and dates match the 2026 CRS and SB 25-276. Opt-in consent for sensitive data, including health condition, gives level 2. No dedicated consumer health data law found in title 6.

freeCopyCases: One free copy to a third-party entity performing duties under the Laura Hershey Disability Support Act, for a disability benefit application, appeal or reapplication (25-1-800.3(3)(b)(I)).
A record not provided within 30 days, or without written notice of a 30-day extension, must be provided at no cost (25-1-801(1)(f)(IV); same rule in 25-1-802).
feeRules: Patient or personal representative: copies on payment of 'the fee a covered entity may impose in accordance with' HIPAA (25-1-801(1)(b)(I)(A)).

Third-party reasonable fees cap: $18.53 for the first ten pages, $0.85 per page for the next thirty, $0.57 per page after; microfilm $1.50 per page; certification $10; actual postage and media costs (25-1-800.3(3)(a)).
Attorney requests over 664 pages: total fees must not exceed $400, inflation-adjusted from 2028 (25-1-801(1)(b)(III), (IV)).
No fee for inspection of records (25-1-801(2)).

provisions.title: Patient records, definitions, free copy for disability benefit claims
provisions.quote: If a patient record is requested by a third-party entity that is performing duties under the "Laura Hershey Disability Support Act", part 2 of article 88 of title 8, the third party may obtain one free copy of the record for the application process
provisions.appliesTo: Applies throughout part 8 of article 1 of title 25 (health-care facilities under 25-1-801 and individual providers under 25-1-802).

provisions.title: Patient records in custody of health-care facility, late records at no cost
provisions.quote: A record not provided within thirty days or without written notification of a thirty-day extension must be provided to the requestor at no cost
provisions.appliesTo: Health facilities licensed under 25-1.5-103(1) or article 3 of title 25 and title 10 entities providing health-care services; the same sentence appears in 25-1-802 for individual providers.

provisions.title: Patient records in custody of health-care facility, copy fee rule
provisions.quote: must provide copies of a patient's medical records, including X rays, to the patient or the patient's personal representative upon request and payment of the fee a covered entity may impose in accordance with the
provisions.appliesTo: Health facilities licensed or certified under 25-1.5-103(1) or article 3 of title 25, and title 10 entities providing health-care services.

provisions.title: Laura Hershey Disability Support Act, sunset review, repeal of part
provisions.quote: This part 2 is repealed, effective July 1, 2027.
provisions.appliesTo: Repeals the act that the free-copy rule in 25-1-800.3(3)(b)(I) cross-references. The amended section took effect 2026-06-02; the repeal takes effect 2027-07-01.

provisions.title: Contexture HIE Opt-In and Opt-Out Information
provisions.citation: Contexture patient opt-in / opt-out policy page
provisions.quote: opting out, your health information will not be accessible through Contexture’s HIE unless the sharing is required by law
provisions.appliesTo: Patients of providers participating in Contexture's HIE in Colorado and Arizona; opt out by signing a form at the provider's office.

provisions.title: Contexture FAQ for Patients, sensitive health information
provisions.quote: Yes, certain types of health information, including substance use information, are subject to additional legal protections.
provisions.appliesTo: Same FAQ states substance use information is available only with the patient's written consent or in a bona fide medical emergency.

hie_consent.note: No Colorado statute on HIE consent found in titles 6 or 25 of the 2026 CRS. The OeHI page names Contexture as the one state-designated HIE. Its published policy is opt-out. Substance use data needs written consent.

crossCheck.note: OeHI names Contexture as the one state-designated HIE. Its published policy is opt-out. No HIE consent statute found in the 2026 CRS index or titles 6 and 25. Substance use data needs written consent.

provisions.title: Prohibition on issuing subpoena in connection with proceeding in another state
provisions.quote: provided that information relating to a medical procedure performed on an individual is not shared with an agency or individual from another state for the purpose of enforcing another state's abortion law.
provisions.appliesTo: Courts, judicial officers, court employees and attorneys issuing subpoenas for out-of-state proceedings about legally protected health-care activity; 13-1-140.1 adds a subpoena affirmation.

reproductive.note: SB 23-188 bars Colorado subpoenas for out-of-state proceedings about legally protected health-care activity and limits sharing procedure information with other states for abortion-law enforcement.

crossCheck.note: 13-1-140 bars Colorado subpoenas for out-of-state proceedings on legally protected health-care activity and limits sharing procedure information with other states. Added by SB 23-188, effective 2023-04-14.

provisions.title: Care and treatment of persons with mental health disorders, records
provisions.quote: all information obtained and records prepared in the course of providing any services to any person pursuant to any provision of this article 65 are confidential and privileged matter.
provisions.appliesTo: Services under article 65 of title 27 (mental health holds, evaluation and treatment). Disclosure is allowed only in listed cases.

mental_health.note: Records of services under article 65 are confidential and privileged and may be disclosed only in listed cases. SB 26-149 added subsections (7) to (12), effective 2026-05-21.

crossCheck.note: Article 65 service records are confidential and privileged and may be disclosed only in listed cases. Lead-in text dates from HB 22-1256. SB 26-149 added (7) to (12), effective 2026-05-21.

provisions.title: Sexually transmitted infections, reports, confidentiality
provisions.quote: any records resulting from compliance with that section held by the state department and county and district public health agencies, or any health-care provider, facility, third-party payer, physician, clinic, laboratory, blood bank, health records database, or other agency, are confidential information.
provisions.appliesTo: "Sexually transmitted infection" refers to chlamydia, syphilis, gonorrhea, HIV, and relevant types of hepatitis (25-4-402(10)).

hiv.note: STI reports and resulting records, which include HIV, are confidential information and may be released only as the section lists. 25-4-406(3) treats STI diagnosis and treatment records as medical information.

provisions.title: Genetic testing, limitations on disclosure of information
provisions.quote: Information derived from genetic testing shall be confidential and privileged. Any release, for purposes other than diagnosis, treatment, or therapy, of genetic testing information that identifies the person tested with the test results released requires specific written consent by the person tested.
provisions.appliesTo: Information derived from genetic testing, as defined in 10-3-1104.7(2).

leads.usedFor: Located section text before reading official CRS

genetic.note: Genetic testing information is confidential and privileged. Release for purposes other than diagnosis, treatment or therapy needs the person's specific written consent.

crossCheck.note: Genetic testing information is confidential and privileged. Release for purposes other than diagnosis, treatment or therapy needs the person's specific written consent. Subsection (3)(a) is unchanged since 1994.

facts.statutoryDamages: Genetic testing (10-3-1104.7(12)): greater of actual damages or $10,000 per violation, plus equitable relief; prevailing party may recover costs and reasonable attorney fees (10-3-1104.7(13)).

provisions.title: Genetic testing, liability
provisions.quote: Any individual who is injured by an entity's violation of this section may recover in a court of competent jurisdiction the following remedies:

provisions.title: Colorado Privacy Act, liability
provisions.quote: this part 13 does not authorize a private right of action for a violation of this part 13 or any other provision of law.
provisions.appliesTo: Colorado Privacy Act controllers and processors.

provisions.title: Notification of security breach, violations
provisions.quote: The attorney general may bring an action in law or equity to address violations of this section, section 6-1-713, or section 6-1-713.5
provisions.appliesTo: Covered entities under the breach statute.

private_right.note: A person may sue only for genetic testing violations under 10-3-1104.7. The Colorado Privacy Act bars a private right of action. The breach statute names the attorney general as enforcer.

crossCheck.note: Suit only for genetic testing violations by group disability or long-term care insurers: actual damages or $10,000 per violation, plus fees. Privacy Act bars suit. Breach law names the attorney general. No broader record right found.
